newsitem.title: HONG KONG: HK stocks inch ahead in morning, off early highs.
newsitem.headline: HK stocks inch ahead in morning, off early highs.

text.p: Hong Kong stocks traded higher in Friday morning trade, helped by gains on Wall Street overnight, but prices were off their early peaks as the market consolidated hefty gains made this week, brokers said.

The Hang Seng Index was up 75.22 points, or 0.54 percent, at 13,905.90. Turnover was HK$4.06 billion after the first 45 minutes of trade. As of Thursday's close, the blue chip index had risen 639.18 points this week.
"The market has to digest the gains," said Geoff Galbraith, institutional sales trader at Nava SC Securities. He expected "no great movements" this session.
Ben Kwong, director of research at Dharmala Securities, said 14,000 points was a major resistance level. The blue-chip index reached an early high of 13,930.66 on Friday.
"The market opened higher following the strength on Wall Street but afterwards there were continued profit-taking pressures. Investors feel 14,000 will be major resistance in the near term," he said.
The Dow industrials ended at a record close on Thursday, up 38.49 points at 6,765.37.
After some consolidation, the Hang Seng Index should be ready to challenge 14,000 points and make a new high, Kwong said. The blue-chip index scored a record intra-day high of 14,004.93 on Thursday.
With futures trading at a discount, Galbraith said the Hang Seng was unlikely to make much headway on Friday. January Hang Seng Index futures were up 105 points at 13,875.
HSBC continued its ascent, rising HK$2.50 to an all-time high of HK$183.50. Analysts said expectations of strong earnings were boosting the stock.
"It has got a lot of covered warrants on it so that accentuates the gains," said Galbraith.
Hang Seng Bank was up HK$1.75 at HK$96.25, while Bank of East Asia inched ahead HK$0.10 to HK$37.00.

Trading in Giordano shares was suspended pending an announcement on the company's business operations in China which it said it had been reviewing. The stock fell HK$1.10, or 17.89 percent, on Thursday to close at HK$5.05.
Trading in Chung Hwa shares was also suspended at the request of the Securities and Futures Commission. The stock, which was also suspended on Thursday, last traded at HK$1.70.
